slot.brief: Three coplanar forces in equilibrium, two at stated angles; resolve along axes and find the magnitude of the third force (keep angles standard like 30°, 60°).

stem: Three coplanar concurrent forces are in equilibrium. Two forces of $6$ N and $8$ N act at angles of $0^\circ$ and $90^\circ$, respectively, to the positive $x$-axis. What is the magnitude of the third force?

verdicts.working: The first two forces have resultant magnitude \(\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10\,\text{N}\). The third force must be equal and opposite to this resultant.

working:
$F_3=\left|-(6\hat{i}+8\hat{j})\right|=\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10\ \text{N}$

Independent check: The first two forces have resultant magnitude \(\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10\,\text{N}\). The third force must be equal and opposite to this resultant.
solution:
For equilibrium, the third force must be equal and opposite to the resultant of the first two forces.
$$F_3=\sqrt{6^2+8^2}=10\,\text{N}$$
